sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and  learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.441 of 2023 pending on the file of learned S.D.J.M., Malkangiri, arising out of Malkangiri P.S. Case No.353 of 2023 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 370/420/34 of IPC read with Section 25 of the Inter- State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979.

entities.text: Inter- State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the co-accused has been released on anticipatory bail by order dated 13.09.2023 in ABLAPL No.8672 of 2023.
Hence, inter alia on the ground of parity, the Petitioner may be protected by pre-arrest bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for pre-arrest bail.

5. Taking into account the nature of allegations, this Court directs that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper subject to verification of criminal antecedent of similar nature.
6. If it comes to the fore that the Petitioner has any such criminal antecedent, this order shall not be given effect to.
7. It is needless to state that the Petitioner shall cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
